sources.title: Batch 0053 exact binary-tree traversal source context
OpenJDK 21 iterative binary-tree traversal deterministic validation

claims.text: The preserved source asks only for an implementation of binary-tree traversal; it does not preserve a language, node API, traversal subset, or recursion requirement.
The candidate explicitly defines Java nodes, null-root behavior, non-mutating preorder/inorder/postorder DFS, and treats level-order BFS only as a conditional follow-up.
The iterative stack implementations produce root-left-right, left-root-right, and left-right-root orders and match independent recursive reference traversals.
Executable validation covers null, an asymmetric directed tree, 2000 deterministic random trees with duplicate values, and a 20000-node skewed tree.

checks: null tree returns empty output for all three traversals
directed asymmetric tree locks preorder/inorder/postorder sequences
2000 deterministic random trees agree with independent recursive oracles
20000-node right-skewed tree completes iteratively without recursive traversal stack dependence

boundary_tests.expected: all iterative traversals complete with 20000 outputs

findings: The candidate respects the sparse repository source and does not invent an externally specified language, API, or traversal subset.
Preorder, inorder, and postorder are all covered with one executable Java class and explicit null-tree behavior.
The postorder explanation correctly identifies completion state as the hard part and uses node identity rather than value equality for lastVisited.
The mechanism section explains iterative traversal as explicit preservation of control state that recursion would otherwise place on the call stack.
OpenJDK 21 validation compares 2000 deterministic random trees against independent recursive oracles and includes a 20000-node skewed tree.
Complexity is stated as O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary stack, with the degenerate h=n case called out rather than assuming balance.
The project section avoids fabricated experience and treats streaming visitor APIs only as a conditional engineering extension.
